model_annotations.Bulgarian: The stacked bar chart illustrates the distribution of experts across 24 model layers, categorized into three groups: G0 (blue), G1 (green), and G2 (yellow), as indicated in the legend. The horizontal axis, labeled “Layer,” spans integer values from 1 to 24, representing sequential model layers, while the vertical axis, labeled “Number of Experts,” is scaled linearly from 0 to 10, indicating the total count of experts per layer. Each bar is composed of three colored segments corresponding to the contribution of each expert group to the total number of experts in that layer. In early layers (e.g., layers 1–5), G2 dominates with the largest segment, followed by G1 and then G0. In mid-layers (e.g., layers 6–18), the contributions become more balanced, with G1 and G2 often comparable and G0 consistently forming the smallest segment. In later layers (e.g., layers 19–22), G1 and G2 again show higher contributions, with G1 often exceeding G2, while G0 remains minimal. Layers 23 and 24 show a reduction in total experts, with G2 and G1 contributing roughly equally and G0 still minimal. The chart visually conveys how expert allocation varies across layers, with no single group dominating uniformly across all layers.
model_annotations.Chinese: This stacked bar chart illustrates the distribution of experts across 24 model layers for a Layer-wise Mixture-of-Experts architecture, comparing three distinct expert groups labeled G0 (blue), G1 (green), and G2 (yellow), as indicated by the legend positioned in the upper center. The horizontal axis, labeled “Layer,” enumerates the 24 layers sequentially from 1 to 24, while the vertical axis, labeled “Number of Experts,” quantifies the total number of active experts per layer, ranging from 0 to 10 with major gridlines at intervals of 2. Each vertical bar represents a single layer and is segmented into colored portions corresponding to the number of experts from each group assigned to that layer. For instance, Layer 1 contains 1 expert from G0, 4 from G1, and 4 from G2, totaling 9 experts. Layer 7 has 1 from G0, 1 from G1, and 1 from G2, summing to 3. In contrast, Layers 19 through 22 each contain 1 from G0, 3 from G1, and 2 from G2, totaling 6 experts per layer. The chart reveals that the total number of experts per layer varies, with some layers (like 1, 2, 4, and 5) hosting as many as 8 or 9 experts, while others (like 7, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 23, and 24) host as few as 3. The composition of expert groups also varies across layers, with G1 consistently contributing the largest segment in most layers, followed by G2, and G0 typically contributing the smallest portion. No explicit sorting or visual emphasis (e.g., shading, bolding, or annotations) is applied to the bars beyond their inherent stacking and color coding.
model_annotations.English: This stacked bar chart illustrates the distribution of experts across 24 layers in a Layer-wise Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, as described in the paper “Less, but Better: Efficient Multilingual Expansion for LLMs via Layer-wise Mixture-of-Experts.” The horizontal axis represents the layer number, ranging from 1 to 24, while the vertical axis indicates the “Number of Experts,” scaled from 0 to 10. Each bar is composed of three colored segments corresponding to three expert groups: G0 (blue), G1 (green), and G2 (yellow), as indicated by the legend. The total height of each bar reflects the total number of experts active in that layer, with the segments showing the contribution of each group. For example, Layer 1 contains 9 total experts: 1 from G0, 4 from G1, and 4 from G2. Layer 7 has the fewest total experts (3), with 1 from G0, 1 from G1, and 1 from G2. Layers 19–22 each have 6 total experts, composed of 1 from G0, 3 from G1, and 2 from G2. The chart reveals a non-uniform distribution, with higher expert counts concentrated in early layers (e.g., Layers 1–5) and later layers (e.g., 19–22), while middle layers (e.g., 10–15) generally have fewer total experts, often around 3. The stacking visually emphasizes how each group contributes to the total per layer, suggesting a strategic allocation of expert capacity across the model’s depth.
model_annotations.German: Das gestapelte Balkendiagramm visualisiert die Verteilung der Anzahl von Experten über 24 aufeinanderfolgende Layer, unterteilt in drei Gruppen: G0 (blau), G1 (grün) und G2 (gelb), wie in der Legende oben rechts angegeben. Die horizontale Achse repräsentiert die Layer, nummeriert von 1 bis 24, und ist linear skaliert. Die vertikale Achse zeigt die „Number of Experts“ mit einem Wertebereich von 0 bis 10, wobei die Skala in Einheiten von 2 unterteilt ist (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10). Jeder Balken entspricht einem Layer und ist in drei farbige Segmente gestapelt, wobei die Höhe jedes Segments die Anzahl der Experten in der jeweiligen Gruppe darstellt. In Layer 1 beträgt die Gesamtzahl der Experten 9, aufgeteilt in 1 (G0), 4 (G1) und 4 (G2). In Layer 2 sind es 8 Experten: 1 (G0), 3 (G1), 4 (G2). In Layer 3: 6 Experten (1 G0, 2 G1, 3 G2). In Layer 4: 8 Experten (1 G0, 3 G1, 4 G2). In Layer 5: 7 Experten (1 G0, 3 G1, 3 G2). In Layer 6: 5 Experten (1 G0, 2 G1, 2 G2). In Layer 7: 3 Experten (1 G0, 1 G1, 1 G2). In Layer 16: 5 Experten (1 G0, 2 G1, 2 G2). In Layer 17: 5 Experten (1 G0, 2 G1, 2 G2). In Layer 18: 5 Experten (1 G0, 2 G1, 2 G2). In Layer 19: 6 Experten (1 G0, 3 G1, 2 G2). In Layer 20: 6 Experten (1 G0, 3 G1, 2 G2). In Layer 21: 6 Experten (1 G0, 3 G1, 2 G2). In Layer 22: 6 Experten (1 G0, 3 G1, 2 G2). In Layer 23: 3 Experten (1 G0, 1 G1, 1 G2). In Layer 24: 3 Experten (1 G0, 1 G1, 1 G2). Die Balken sind in der Reihenfolge der Layer nummeriert und nicht nach Höhe oder Wert sortiert; es gibt keine visuellen Hervorhebungen wie Schattierungen oder Umrandungen.
